title: Frozen direct six-core remainder verification
status: Declared before domain enumeration or exact six-core evaluation; coordinator-approved.
derivation: Inherited widest four-core windows and T2(b,c)<w_a certify positivity outside the listed36(a,b) branches. Any remaining c is <=62. Strict sixth/seventh anchors and one-sided eighth anchors remove further branches. No unique-seven-divisor shortcut or newly tailored pair windows are used to prune this protocol.
domain_rule: For every declared(a,b), take integers b<c<=62, with c outside{1,4,5}.
Retain iff at least one of a,b,c is divisible by6 and at least one is divisible by7.
Retain iff either at least one of a,b,c is divisible by8 OR their residues mod8 contain both3and7.
Sort retained triples lexicographically. This fixed formula is the complete evaluated domain, with no optional extra cases.
outputs: all maximal closed safe components, including isolated points
positive component count and isolated point count
earliest widest positive component and all ties, or null if none
exact selected endpoint and midpoint distances for all six speeds
ceil(1/(4*w)) one-additional-runner sufficient cutoff when w>0
independent_method: Independently generate the same declared domain; modular predicates at every rational threshold and open-cell midpoint, then reconstruct maximal components. No primary code or output access until independent output is frozen.
comparison: Match the complete domains and all common mathematical fields; separately verify that the archived w_a values and36 branches support the analytic reduction.
limits: No refinement of the frozen domain after results
A failed positivity row must be retained and investigated; do not patch the protocol to hide it
General proof remains HYPOTHESIS/proof candidate; exact records OBSERVED
stopping_rule: Complete this domain and independent comparison, then stop evaluation. Any additional concrete case requires a separately declared protocol.
